text:
alex wang: Hey team — first week setup hiccup. I spun up docker compose with profiles but my app container can't reach Postgres at db:5432. Error: "could not translate host name "db"". I'm on mac (Apple Silicon) and using Docker Desktop.

alex wang: My compose.yml (redacted):
```yaml
version: "3.9"
services:
  app:
    build: .
    profiles: ["local"]
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pass@db:5432/app
  db:
    image: postgres:14
    profiles: ["db"]
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pass
```

alex wang: I ran `docker compose --profile local up --build` because I thought the db would come up too. Any obvious dumb mistake? :sweat_smile:

sara patel: hey alex — small gotcha: profiles are opt-in. running with `--profile local` only enables services with profile `local`, so `db` (profile `db`) never started. That's why the DNS name `db` doesn't exist. Try `docker compose --profile local --profile db up` or just `docker compose up` for dev. :thumbsup:

ben thomas: another quick check: `docker compose ps` will show which services are running. also `docker compose logs db` to see if db started and is healthy. `depends_on` doesn't wait for postgres to accept connections, only for container start — you'll still want a wait script if your app needs db immediately.

alex wang: ohh that explains it. I did `ps` earlier but missed that db wasn't listed. will re-run with both profiles. thanks!

ben thomas: if you want a one-liner to bring both up: `docker compose --profile db --profile local up -d --build` then `docker compose logs -f db` to watch migrations. Also you can add a simple healthcheck to db in compose: 
```yaml
  db:
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 3s
      retries: 5
```
This helps containers that inspect health, and you can `wait-for` that in your entrypoint.

alex wang: adding healthcheck now. quick question — does Docker Desktop on Apple Silicon need any extra flags for postgres image? I saw some posts about arch compatibility.

sara patel: postgres:14 multi-arch should be fine. only thing is image may run under emulation for some rare tags. if you hit weird startup failures check `docker compose logs db` — common problems are volume permissions (if you mount host dir) or older WAL files. If using a host mount for PGDATA, chown to 999:999 or use a named volume.

infra-bot: Reminder: new-hires/dev checklist — if you hit persistent volume issues, see https://redwood.internal/devenv/storage for recommended compose snippets and mac-specific notes.

alex wang: confirmed — `docker compose --profile db --profile local up` fixed it. db came up, app connected. closing ticket, huge thanks! :rocket:
